reasons: Failures are hidden, which makes problems hard to notice.

terms.meaning: A list file that names what content is available.
A short, web-friendly name for a project, used in its address.
A saved result kept so the same request is not repeated.
A rating of how ready the code is for real use.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and imports
sections.what: Explains what the component is for and where its list comes from. Loads the helper code it needs and sets up one shared place to keep the loaded list.
sections.why: The top comment records that the list comes from the publishing tool, so a maintainer knows where to look.
sections.watch_out: The manifest is written by an outside command. If that command changes the shape of its output, this code will quietly treat the list as empty.

sections.name: loadCodeManifest
sections.title: Loading the explorer list once
sections.what: Downloads the manifest the first time it is needed and keeps the result. If the file is missing or broken, it returns an empty list.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared download avoids asking for the same file again for every project link on a page.
sections.watch_out: The saved result is never cleared, so a short network problem stays in place until the visitor reloads the page.

sections.name: CodeExplorerLink
sections.title: The link itself
sections.what: Looks up this project's entry and shows nothing if none exists. Otherwise shows a header link, or a block with the number of explained files, the section count, a readiness label, a privacy note for private projects, and links to the explorer and its technical map.
sections.why: Keeps dead links off project pages while still showing how much of the code has been explained.
sections.watch_out: The readiness label comes from a lookup table. A readiness value not in that table is shown as not checked.

summary: A small link that appears on a project page only when that project has a published code explorer.
purpose: Connects a project page to its code explorer and stays hidden when there is no explorer yet.
why: The explorer list is produced by a separate publishing command, so each page must check for it when it loads. The file comment says pages should never show a dead link.
how: Loads the explorer list once and keeps the result for the rest of the visit. Finds the entry for this project. Then it shows either a small header link, a larger block with counts and a readiness label, or nothing.
inputs: The project slug, the display style (header or section), and the manifest file at the public code folder.
outputs: Nothing, a header link, or a section block with explained file counts, section count, a readiness label, a privacy note, and links to the explorer and its technical map.
risks: A failed download of the list is treated as an empty list, so the link quietly never appears. The list is cached for the whole visit, so a failure is not retried until the page reloads.
debug: If a link is missing, check that the manifest file has an entry whose project value matches the slug. Check that the explorer folder exists. Check the browser's network view for the manifest request and its status.
